subtitle.en: Mapping the walkable surfaces on the island of The Witness as a step toward bulletproofing the player movement code.
subtitle.zh: 把整座岛的可行走表面测绘出来，作为「让玩家移动代码坚不可摧」的第一步。

translator.note: 本篇是全站的风格基准样例：段落逐一对齐，代码原样保留，图片未收录（原文有 14 张示意图，可回原文查看）。

blocks.en: Despite not even being finished, [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) is already one of my all-time favorite games.  I've been playing it since [Jonathan Blow](http://number-none.com/blow/) started developing it several years ago, and I could not be more excited about its upcoming release.
blocks.zh: 尽管《The Witness》还没做完，它已经是我有史以来最喜欢的游戏之一。从 [Jonathan Blow](http://number-none.com/blow/) 几年前开始开发它起，我就一直在玩，我对它的发售再期待不过了。

blocks.en: Unlike Jon's previous game [Braid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braid_%28video_game%29), the asset and programming scale for [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) is much further toward the "triple-A" side of the scale than the "indie game" side.  As anyone who works on these types of projects knows, the work required to successfully pull off a game goes up dramatically when you go that direction.  [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) already has several more people working on it than [Braid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braid_%28video_game%29) did at its peak, but as with any project of this size, there are still many parts of the project that need more attention than the principals can afford to give them.
blocks.zh: 和 Jon 的前作 [Braid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braid_%28video_game%29) 不同，《The Witness》在美术资产与程序规模上都更靠近「3A」那一端，而不是「独立游戏」那一端。做过这类项目的人都清楚：一旦往那个方向走，要把游戏真正做出来所需的工作量会急剧上升。《The Witness》的团队规模已经比 Braid 巅峰期多出好几个人，但和任何这种体量的项目一样，总有许多部分需要投入的精力超出了核心成员能给出的上限。

blocks.en: For this reason, it was always my intention to try to find some time to help out on [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) when it came time to ship it.  So this past Thanksgiving, Jon and I sat down and he went through a list of things in the codebase that he thought would benefit from the attention of an extra programmer.  After considering the relative importance of the items, we decided that the player movement code was the place where improvements could have the biggest impact on the player's experience.
blocks.zh: 正因如此，我一直打算在《The Witness》临近发售时挤出点时间来帮把手。所以去年感恩节，Jon 和我坐下来，他过了一遍代码库里那些他认为「值得多一个程序员来处理」的事项清单。权衡了各项的相对重要性之后，我们认定：玩家移动代码是改进之后对玩家体验影响最大的地方。
名字来自 Quake 的报错
blocks.en: Walkmonster in Wall

In the context of [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/), the goal of player movement code is to be as unobtrusive as possible.  The player is supposed to fully immerse themselves in an alternate reality, and every last detail is important to this experience.  The last thing you ever want to happen is to have the player notice the fact that they're sitting at a computer asking it to move a virtual viewpoint around.
blocks.zh: 在《The Witness》的语境里，玩家移动代码的目标是尽可能不引人注意。玩家本应完全沉浸在一个替代现实之中，每一个细节对这种体验都很重要。你最不希望发生的事，就是让玩家意识到自己正坐在电脑前、指挥一个虚拟视点四处移动。

blocks.en: For that reason, the player movement code has to be rock solid.  If you can get stuck on edges, trapped in walls, fall through the floor, walk through a cliff, walk down a hill but not back up it, etc., it immediately breaks the immersion and reminds you that you are playing an artificial experience mitigated by an unreliable system.  It can also lead to disastrous consequences for the player in some circumstances if there's no way for them to recover from the problem with restarting or reloading a (possibly very old) save game.  If you play games often, you've probably encountered one or more of these problems in shipping titles, and you know what I'm talking about.
blocks.zh: 正因如此，玩家移动代码必须坚如磐石。如果你会被卡在边缘、困在墙里、掉穿地板、穿过悬崖、能走下坡却走不上来——沉浸感立刻破碎，它会提醒你：你正在玩的是一个由不可靠系统所中介的人造体验。在某些情况下，如果玩家除了重启或者读取（可能是很久以前的）存档之外毫无办法，这还会带来灾难性的后果。如果你经常玩游戏，多半在已发售的作品里遇到过一个或多个这类问题，你明白我在说什么。

blocks.en: Last week I began to work on this problem.  I decided the first thing to do was to write a few integrated tools for working with the player movement code so we could analyze it and see how it was currently behaving.  Immediately, when I opened up the project, I found myself with a familiar conundrum: what to name my first source file.  This is always the most important part of any project ([as Bob Pollard once said of band names and album names](http://www.gbv.com/inter4.html)).  If you have the right name for your source file, it's smooth sailing from there.  Pick the wrong name, and you might as well call the project off.
blocks.zh: 上周我开始处理这个问题。我决定第一件事是先写几个和玩家移动代码配套的工具，好让我们能分析它、看清它当前的行为。一打开项目，我立刻遇上了一个熟悉的难题：第一个源文件该叫什么名字。这一向是任何项目里最重要的部分（[正如 Bob Pollard 谈起乐队名和专辑名时说的那样](http://www.gbv.com/inter4.html)）。源文件名起对了，后面就一帆风顺；起错了，那这项目不如直接取消。

blocks.en: But what to call a system for bulletproofing player movement code?  I'd never been asked to write code for that before.  When I thought about it, I realized that I'd only personally seen evidence of similar code once before: when playing an early beta of [Quake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quake_(video_game)).  There were some bugs with the monster placement, and in the console window, you could see error messages announcing the fact that the monsters, instead of spawning on the ground, had spawned partially intersecting with the level geometry.  Each debug message began with the phrase "walkmonster in wall at…"
blocks.zh: 可是，一个用来「给玩家移动代码穿防弹衣」的系统该叫什么？我以前从没被要求写过这种东西。想来想去，我意识到自己只见过一次类似的代码：玩早期 beta 版 [Quake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quake_(video_game)) 的时候。当时怪物放置出了 bug，控制台窗口里能看到报错信息，说怪物没有生成在地面上，而是和关卡几何体有部分穿插。每条调试信息的开头都是那句「walkmonster in wall at…」。

blocks.en: Bingo.  It's hard to ask for a better source file name than "walk_monster.cpp".  I was pretty sure, from that point forward, the code was going to come along nicely.
blocks.zh: 就是它了。很难找到比 `walk_monster.cpp` 更好的源文件名。我当时就很确定：从这一刻起，这份代码会写得顺风顺水。
DriveTowardPoint：真的去测试系统
blocks.en: Drive Toward Point
When you're trying to test a system, the most important thing to do is *actually test the system*.  Even though that sounds like a straightforward rule, people writing tests often fail to observe it.
blocks.zh: 当你要测试一个系统时，最重要的事情就是*真的去测试这个系统*。这话听起来直白得很，但写测试的人经常做不到。

blocks.en: In this specific case, there are very easy ways to *think* that you were testing the player movement code without actually testing it.  One example would be to do some kind of analysis on the collision volumes and walkable surfaces in the game, looking for small areas, gaps, etc.  Once you'd eliminated all of these, you'd then proclaim the world safe to traverse and move on.
blocks.zh: 在这个具体场景里，有很容易让人*误以为*自己在测试移动代码的做法。比如：对游戏里的碰撞体和可行走表面做某种分析，去找小面积区域、缝隙之类的东西。把这些都清理干净之后，你就宣布这个世界可以安全通行，然后收工。

blocks.en: But this is testing the data, not the actual code.  It's still easily possible to have bugs in the movement code that result in bad behavior even with sanitized data.
blocks.zh: 但这是在测数据，不是在测代码。即使数据是干净的，移动代码里依然很容易存在导致错误行为的 bug。

blocks.en: To avoid this kind of trap, I wanted the testing system to remain as close as possible to what a human does to actually control player movement in the game.  I started out by writing two routines to serve as the building blocks of this kind of testing.
blocks.zh: 为了避开这类陷阱，我希望测试系统尽可能贴近「真人在游戏里实际操作玩家移动」这件事。于是我一开始就写了两个例程，作为这类测试的积木。

blocks.en: The first is the closest to real human usage.  It's an update call that hooks into [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/)'s input processing and feeds it synthetic mouse and keyboard events.  It can do some basic things that humans might do, such as looking around, walking toward a point, looking toward a point, and so on.  It does these through nothing but emulation of human interaction with the mouse and keyboard, so I know that everything in [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/)'s input path will be running as it actually would during testing.  I'll talk more about this system and how it's used in later installments.
blocks.zh: 第一个最接近真人操作。它是一个 update 调用，挂进《The Witness》的输入处理流程，往里喂合成的鼠标与键盘事件。它能做人类会做的一些基本动作——四处张望、朝某点走过去、把视线转向某点等等。而这些动作*全部*只通过模拟人类对鼠标键盘的操作来实现，所以我可以确信：《The Witness》输入路径上的每一段代码，在测试时都会按它真实运行的方式跑起来。这个系统以及它的用法，我会在后面几篇里细说。

blocks.en: The second piece of code is one step removed from that level.  It's a function called *DriveTowardPoint* that takes two points in the world and, calling the existing player collision system, attempts to move cleanly from one to the other.  When it returns, it provides information about the attempt such as obstacles encountered and whether or not the destination was successfully reached.
blocks.zh: 第二段代码则比那个层次远了一步。它是一个叫 *DriveTowardPoint* 的函数：接收世界里的两个点，调用现有的玩家碰撞系统，尝试干净地从一点移动到另一点。返回时会带上这次尝试的信息，比如途中遇到了哪些障碍、是否成功抵达目标。

blocks.en: This function is not quite as reliable as the synthetic input method of testing, because it eliminates a portion of the actual player movement system from testing.  For example, any erroneous state associated with where the player is that the collision system might have built up won't affect tests using this function.  Nevertheless, I felt it valuable to have this level of testing available because it can much more rapidly test large areas, since it does not require the entire game loop to run, and thus can be employed much more frequently and over the entire world instead of just isolated test runs.
blocks.zh: 这个函数不如合成输入那种测法可靠，因为它把真实玩家移动系统的一部分排除在测试之外了。举例来说，碰撞系统可能累积起来的、与玩家位置有关的错误状态，就不会影响用这个函数做的测试。尽管如此，我还是觉得有这么一层测试很有价值：它不需要跑完整的游戏主循环，因此能快得多地测试大片区域，也就能更频繁地使用、覆盖整个世界，而不是只做一些孤立的测试运行。

blocks.en: It's also worth noting that there are no physics inputs to this function; there are no velocities specified for the starting point, for example.  This is because *The Witness* is not an action game, so there are few stateful physical properties for the player.  Players can't jump, they can't wall-run, they can't enter bullet-time. Supporting these types of behaviors is possible with systems of the kind I'll be discussing, but they add a layer of complexity that we don't have to worry about on this project.
blocks.zh: 还有一点值得说明：这个函数没有任何物理输入，比如起点没有指定速度。原因是《The Witness》不是动作游戏，玩家身上几乎没有什么带状态的物理属性。玩家不能跳、不能蹬墙跑、也不能进入子弹时间。用我接下来要讲的这类系统去支持这些行为是可行的，但它们会多出一层复杂度，而这个项目不必操心。

blocks.en: Anyhow, with *DriveTowardPoint* in place, it was possible for me to start on my first goal for the system: determining everywhere the player can go on the island of *The Witness*.
blocks.zh: 总之，有了 *DriveTowardPoint*，我就可以开始实现这个系统的第一个目标了：弄清玩家在《The Witness》的岛上究竟能去到哪些地方。
快速扩展随机树
blocks.en: Rapidly Exploring Random Trees

Where can the player go?  It seems like a simple question, but you'd be surprised how many games ship without the development team knowing the real answer.  If possible, I want [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) to be one of the few games where the team knows prior to shipping exactly where the player can and can't go, no surprises.
blocks.zh: 玩家能去哪？这看着是个简单问题，但你会惊讶于有多少游戏在发售时，开发团队并不知道真正的答案。如果可能，我希望《The Witness》成为少数几个「团队在发售前就确切知道玩家能去哪、不能去哪」的游戏——没有意外。

blocks.en: This makes the problem statement, but perhaps not the problem, very simple: given a *DriveTowardPoint* function that faithfully determines whether a player could move in a straight line between two points, produce a coverage map showing everywhere the player could end up.
blocks.zh: 这让问题的*表述*变得非常简单（但问题本身未必简单）：给定一个能忠实判断「玩家能否沿直线从一点移动到另一点」的 *DriveTowardPoint* 函数，产出一张覆盖图，显示玩家可能抵达的所有位置。

blocks.en: For reasons that I can't necessarily explain, I had in my head, even before writing a line of code, that the best way to do this would be to use a [Rapidly Exploring Random Tree](http://msl.cs.uiuc.edu/rrt).  For those of you unfamiliar with this algorithm, it's a very simple process whereby you record all the points you've visited along with a reference to the point from which you walked there.  To add points to the tree, you pick a random target point anywhere in the world, select the closest point in your tree thus far, and try to get from that tree point to the target point.  Wherever you end up, that's a new sample point.
blocks.zh: 出于一些我自己也说不清的原因，在写第一行代码之前，我脑子里就已经认定最好的做法是用[快速扩展随机树](http://msl.cs.uiuc.edu/rrt)（RRT）。不熟悉这个算法的话，它的过程非常简单：记录所有你走过的点，同时记下你是从哪个点走到那里的。要往树里加点时，就在世界里随便挑一个随机目标点，选出目前树中离它最近的点，然后试着从那个树点走到目标点。你最终停在哪里，哪里就是一个新的采样点。

blocks.en: Normally, this is more of a pathfinding algorithm, so interleaved with random points, you repeatedly select some goal point as a target.  This biases the exploration of the space toward the target, which is what you want when your only aim is to reach the goal.  But in this case, I wanted to produce a complete map of everywhere the player could go, so I was exclusively using random samples.
blocks.zh: 通常它更像一个寻路算法，所以除了随机点，你还会反复把某个目标点当作靶子。这会让空间探索偏向目标方向——当你唯一的目的就是抵达终点时，这正是你想要的。但在这里，我要产出的是「玩家能去的所有地方」的完整地图，所以我只用了纯随机采样。

blocks.en: After implementing this (it is thankfully a very simple algorithm to write, so it doesn't take long), I could see that it did do a reasonable job of exploring the space (the white etchings show paths that have been explored, and the red vertical lines show places where an obstacle was hit):
blocks.zh: 实现之后（谢天谢地，这个算法写起来非常简单，花不了多少时间），我能看出它确实还算像样地探索了空间（白色的刻痕是被探索过的路径，红色竖线是撞到障碍的地方）：

blocks.en: However, once I actually looked at how it behaved, it was clear to me that it wasn't really the algorithm I wanted.  For example, even after many iterations, it often barely explores rooms like this one, despite densely covering the area just outside, simply because it doesn't pick enough random targets inside it:
blocks.zh: 但真正看了它的行为之后，我清楚地意识到它并不是我想要的算法。比如，即使迭代很多次，它经常几乎不进这种房间，尽管房间外面那一带被覆盖得很密——原因很简单：它在房间内部挑到的随机目标点不够多：

blocks.en: If I'd thought about it before I started, I would have realized that the benefit of something like a Rapidly Exploring Random Tree is that it explores high-dimensional spaces efficiently.  In fact that's the primary reason you normally use it.  But in [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/), we don't have a high-dimensional space.  We have a two-dimensional space (distributed on an intricate manifold, yes, but a two-dimensional space nonetheless).
blocks.zh: 如果我在动手前先想清楚，就会明白 RRT 这类算法的优势在于**高效探索高维空间**——这其实正是人们平常使用它的首要理由。但在《The Witness》里，我们要处理的不是高维空间，而是一个二维空间（是的，它分布在一个精巧的流形上，但终究还是二维的）。

blocks.en: In this low-dimensional space, the benefits of a Rapidly Exploring Random Tree are muted, and the drawback is critically bad for my stated purpose: it's designed to most efficiently find ways to connect pairs of points in a space, not to efficiently find all reachable points in that space.  If you care about the latter, then Rapidly Exploring Random Trees will actually take an excruciatingly long time to do so.
blocks.zh: 在低维空间里，RRT 的好处被削弱了，而它的短板对我的目标来说却是致命地糟糕：它被设计来*最高效地找到连接空间中一对点的路径*，而不是*高效地找出该空间中所有可达的点*。如果你要的是后者，RRT 实际上会花掉漫长得令人痛苦的时间。

blocks.en: So, I quickly realized that what I should be looking for is an algorithm that efficiently covers low-dimensional spaces in their entirety.
blocks.zh: 于是我很快意识到：我真正要找的，是一种能高效地*完整覆盖低维空间*的算法。
三维洪泛填充
blocks.en: 3D Flood Filling

Once I actually thought about the choice of algorithm, it seemed obvious that what I actually wanted was something like the old 2D flood fills we used to use to fill regions of a bitmap.  Given a starting point, I just wanted to fill up the entire space, exhaustively probing every possible way you could go.  Unfortunately, this is a lot less straightforward in the world of [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) than it is in a 2D bitmap, for a number of reasons.
blocks.zh: 一旦真的开始思考算法选择，答案就显而易见了：我想要的其实就是当年给位图区域填色用的那种二维洪泛填充。给定一个起点，把整个空间填满，穷尽地探查每一条可能走的路。可惜在《The Witness》的世界里，这比在位图上做要困难得多，原因有好几个。

blocks.en: First, there's no clear concept of finite connectivity around a point.  Everything is continuous.  It's not like pixels where you can easily enumerate 4 possible places to go from every given location, and check each one in turn.
blocks.zh: 第一，一个点周围「有限个连接」这个概念并不成立，一切都是连续的。它不像像素：在每个位置你都能轻松列举出 4 个可走的方向，然后逐个检查。

blocks.en: Second, there's no fixed size for a locus in space like there is for a pixel in a bitmap.  Walkable surfaces and obstacles can be anywhere, they have no minimum or maximum feature size, and no alignment to any external grid.
blocks.zh: 第二，空间中的一个「位置」没有像位图里像素那样的固定尺寸。可行走表面和障碍可以出现在任何地方，它们的特征尺寸既没有下限也没有上限，也不对齐任何外部网格。

blocks.en: Third, although walking around in [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) locally acts as if it were on a plane, the space itself actually is a deeply interconnected and varying manifold, with walkable regions directly above other regions (stacked perhaps several times over), and special connectivity that changes based on world states (such as doors that open, elevators that go up and down, etc.
blocks.zh: 第三，虽然在《The Witness》里走动时局部表现像是在一个平面上，但空间本身其实是一个深度互联、形式多变的流形：可行走区域可能正压在另一些区域上方（也许叠了好几层），而且连通性还会随世界状态变化（比如会打开的门、上下运行的升降机，等等）。

blocks.en: Given these complexities, it is very easy to think you have devised a way to do a flood fill, only to find after you've implemented it that it gets bogged down oversampling areas, misses important paths, produces erroneous connectivity information at places where the manifold is complex, or is simply too cumbersome to use because it must be restarted to cope with changes in the world state.
blocks.zh: 有了这些复杂之处，你很容易以为自己想出了一种做洪泛填充的办法，实现之后才发现：它陷在过度采样里拔不出来、漏掉重要的通路、在流形复杂的地方给出错误的连通信息，或者因为世界状态一变就得整个重来而变得根本没法用。

blocks.en: No good solution to all of this immediately came to mind, so I tried some simple experimentation.  Using the [Rapidly Exploring Random Tree](http://msl.cs.uiuc.edu/rrt) code I had written, I changed the target point selection from random selection to a very controlled selection.  Each time a new point was added to the tree, I would say that points a unit step along the cardinal directions from that point where to be considered future targets, just like a basic 2D flood fill.
blocks.zh: 我并没有立刻想到能解决所有这些问题的好办法，于是先做了些简单的实验。我用已经写好的 RRT 代码，把目标点的选取从随机改成完全受控：每当一个新点加入树中，我就把从该点沿四个基本方向走一个单位步长得到的点，作为后续的目标点——就像最基础的二维洪泛填充那样。

blocks.en: But of course, this would produce a useless sampling loop if I wasn't careful.  A point would branch out to a neighborhood of 8 points around it, but those 8 points would all then want to try the original point again, and this would go back and forth forever.  So in addition to the controlled target selection, I also needed the simple constraint that any target which wasn't some minimum useful distance away from an existing target point would not be considered.  To my surprise, these two rather simple rules did produce a somewhat usable flood fill:
blocks.zh: 但当然，一不小心就会变成毫无意义的采样死循环：一个点向周围 8 个邻点扩散，而这 8 个点又都想回头去试原来那个点，来回无穷无尽。所以在受控选取目标之外，我还需要一条简单约束：任何与已有目标点距离不足某个最小有效距离的候选点，都不予考虑。出乎我意料的是，这两条相当简单的规则确实产出了一个勉强能用的洪泛填充：

blocks.en: Not bad for just trying the obvious thing.  But it suffers from what I've taken to calling "boundary echo".  You can see this effect in the following screenshot, taken while the map exploration was still in progress:
blocks.zh: 对「先试试最显然的做法」来说，这不算差。但它有一个我称之为「边界回声」（boundary echo）的毛病。下面这张截图是在地图探索还在进行时拍的，能看到这个效应：

blocks.en: In regions with no obstacles, this algorithm proceeds nicely, sampling at a relatively even distance.  But once it hits a boundary, the intersections there produce points that are "off grid", in that they are not aligned along the sampling pattern with which the algorithm filled the adjacent open region.  The reason "on grid" points don't produce overly dense tessellation is because any new point that tries to step back onto one of the previous points finds the previous point there and declines to reconsider it.  But when new points are produced on the boundary, they are completely unaligned, so there is nothing to stop them from stepping back into the already explored space.  This creates a wave of offset sampling which will continue until it runs into a fortuitous line of points somewhere else that happen to be close enough to its advancing front for it to consider them coincident.
blocks.zh: 在没有障碍的区域里，这个算法进行得很顺，采样间距相对均匀。可一旦撞上边界，那里的交点就会产生一批「脱格」的点——它们不再沿着算法填充相邻开阔区域时所用的采样格局排列。「在格上」的点之所以不会造成过密的细分，是因为任何想往回踩到已有采样点上的新点，都会在那里发现那个旧点，从而放弃重复考虑它。但边界上产生的新点是完全不对齐的，于是没有任何东西能阻止它们再踩回已经探索过的空间。这就形成了一道偏移采样的波前，它会一直推进，直到在别处碰巧撞上一排点——那排点恰好离它推进的前沿足够近，足以被判定为重合，它才停下来。

blocks.en: Although this may not seem like a huge problem, it is actually critical.  The entire goal of an algorithm like this is to concentrate the samples in the areas where they are most likely to yield productive results.  The more time you spend sampling and resampling wide open regions, the less time you spend mapping the actual edges of that region, which is the information you actually wanted.  Because this is a continuous space and only an infinite number of samples can truly reveal its exact shape, your ratio of meaningful to meaningless samples is literally the measure of how effective your algorithm is at producing the walkable area.
blocks.zh: 这看起来也许不算大问题，但实际上非常关键。这类算法的全部目的，就是**把采样集中在最可能产生有用结果的地方**。你在空旷区域上采样、重复采样花的时间越多，用来测绘那片区域真实边界的时间就越少——而边界才是你真正想要的信息。由于这是连续空间，只有无限多的采样才能真正揭示它的确切形状，所以「有意义的采样」与「无意义的采样」之比，正是衡量你这个算法在产出可行走区域上有多有效的指标。

blocks.en: Now, there is an easy fix for this specific problem: expand the distance at which two points are considered "close enough".  But by doing this to reduce sampling density in places you *don't* care about, you lose sampling density in places you *do* care about, like around boundaries where you are trying to carefully probe for holes.
blocks.zh: 针对这个具体问题，有个简单的修法：把判定两点「足够近」的距离阈值调大。但你为了降低*不*关心的区域里的采样密度而这么做时，也会连带失去*确实*关心的区域里的采样密度——比如边界周围，那正是你想仔细探查有没有漏洞的地方。
局部方向性采样
blocks.en: Localized Directional Sampling

Perhaps because I had started with a Rapidly Exploring Random Tree, my brain had been pigeonholed into thinking about proximity to the exclusion of everything else.  The previous algorithms had all been about using proximity to do things, like figure out whether a new point should be considered, or which point to start from when trying to get to a new target point.
blocks.zh: 也许是因为我从 RRT 起步，我的脑子被关进了「只考虑距离」的笼子里，把别的东西全排除了。前面那些算法都依赖距离来做判断：判断一个新点该不该被采纳，或者去往某个新目标时该从哪个点出发。

blocks.en: But after thinking about the problem for a while, I came to realize is that everything falls more neatly into place if you think in terms of *directionality* as well as proximity.  While obvious in hindsight, if you've worked on these sorts of problems before, you know it's easy to get trapped in one way of thinking for a while and not see the bigger picture, even if it turns out to be a simple one.  That is precisely what had happened to me.
blocks.zh: 但想了一阵之后，我意识到：只要在距离之外也考虑*方向性*，一切就都归位得更整齐了。这话事后看显而易见，但如果你以前做过这类问题，就知道人很容易在一段时间里陷进某一种思路，看不到更大的图景——哪怕那图景其实很简单。我遇到的正是这种情况。

blocks.en: Once I shifted perspective, the correct sampling behavior was obvious.  Each time I wanted to expand the exploration from a point, I would do a proximity query for a local neighborhood of existing nearby points.  Instead of using the distance to those points to guide the exploration, however, I would categorize them by their direction (currently, I just use the eight cardinal directions, but I'd like to experiment with different kernels here).
blocks.zh: 视角一换，正确的采样行为就一目了然了。每次我想从某个点向外扩展探索时，就先做一次邻近查询，取出它周围已有的那圈点。但接下来，我不是用「到这些点的距离」来引导探索，而是**按方向给它们归类**（目前我只用了八个基本方向，不过我很想在这里试试不同的核）。

blocks.en: In any direction where I don't "see" a point, I walk a predetermined distance and add a point wherever I end up (whether I hit something or not).  In any direction where I do see a point, I walk there and make sure I can get to it.  If I can, I just add a visible edge, so it's easy for the user to see that we're connected.  If I can't, then I do add a new point at the collision, revealing the obstacle boundary.
blocks.zh: 在任何一个方向上看不到已有点时，我就朝那里走一段预定距离，无论最终停在哪里（不管有没有撞到东西）都在那里加一个点。在任何一个方向上看到了已有点时，我就走过去，确认自己确实能到达；如果能，就只加一条可见的边，这样使用者一眼就能看出这两点是连通的；如果不能，我就在碰撞处加一个新点，把障碍边界暴露出来。

blocks.en: This sampling method works beautifully.  It allows you to very accurately control the sampling with nicely tunable parameters, keeping all the points you want while preventing unnecessary tesselation, which leads to a very fast filling of the space:
blocks.zh: 这个采样方法效果极好。它让你能用几个好调的参数非常精确地控制采样：该留的点都留着，同时避免不必要的细分，于是空间填充得非常快：

blocks.en: Because it searches along directions rather than just using proximity, it is immune to boundary echo, and restricts oversampling to the boundaries where you actually want it:
blocks.zh: 由于它是沿方向搜索而不只是靠距离，它对边界回声免疫，并且把过度采样限制在你真正需要它的边界上：

blocks.en: Furthermore, it's completely impervious to state changes or complex manifold problems.  It deals strictly with points and those points can be anywhere, and you can add new ones at any time.  If you've already made a map of an area with a door closed, and you open the door, all you have to do is plant a single new exploration point on the other side of the door and say "continue expanding this map", and it'll connect itself back up and explore the entire area beyond the door properly.
blocks.zh: 更进一步，它对世界状态变化或复杂的流形问题完全无所谓。它只跟点打交道，而点可以在任何地方，你也可以随时加新点。如果你已经在一扇门关着的状态下把一片区域测绘完了，之后门打开了，你只需要在门的另一侧种下一个新的探索点，然后说一句「继续扩展这张地图」，它就会自己接回去，把门后那片区域完整地探索一遍。

blocks.en: You can also change any of the core parameters at any time, and everything still works.  Want to sample an area more densely?  Just set the default spacing lower.  You can do this in the middle of a map build, and it will start sampling more densely, with no need to jettison the existing results (which may have taken some time to produce).
blocks.zh: 你也可以随时修改任何核心参数，整套东西照样运转。想让某片区域采样得更密？把默认间距调小就行。你可以在一次地图构建的途中这么做，它会立刻开始更密地采样，而不需要抛弃已有的结果（那些结果可能花了不少时间才产出）。
初步的边界探查
blocks.en: Rudimentary Edge Probing

Although the algorithm by default will already sample boundaries more thoroughly, because intersections produce additional points beyond the sampling pattern, it didn't necessarily probe them as thoroughly as I wanted, because it doesn't do anything special when it encounters obstacles.  It occurred to me that since I know which points were produced from collisions and which were not, whenever two collision points found themselves connected by an edge, I could choose to invoke extra sampling to try to find more boundary points nearby.
blocks.zh: 虽然得益于「碰撞会产生采样格局之外的新点」，这个算法默认就已经把边界采得比较密了，但它探测边界的细致程度未必达到我想要的，因为它在遇到障碍时并没有做任何特殊处理。我想到：既然我知道哪些点是由碰撞产生的、哪些不是，那么每当两个碰撞点之间连上了一条边，我就可以选择额外触发一轮采样，试着找出附近更多的边界点。

blocks.en: I haven't yet worked on this extensively, but I put in a rudimentary method to test the theory, and it shows promise.  For any two collision points connected by an edge, I step to the midpoint of the edge and probe outwards perpendicular to the edge.  If I don't collide with the boundary within a very short distance, I assume that the boundary is more complex, and add a new target there so the search will continue in that area.
blocks.zh: 这块我还没有深入做，但先实现了一个很初级的办法来验证想法，结果看起来有前途。对于任意两个由一条边相连的碰撞点，我走到这条边的中点，然后沿垂直于该边的方向向外探查。如果在很短的距离内没有撞到边界，我就认为这里的边界更复杂，于是在那里加一个新的目标点，让搜索继续在这一带进行。

blocks.en: Even this simple scheme produces nicely dense sampling along the boundary, without any oversampling of open regions nearby.  Here's a region with several boundaries, but without edge probing:
blocks.zh: 即便这么简单的方案，也能沿着边界得到相当不错的密集采样，而且完全没有对附近的开阔区域过度采样。下面这张是没开边界探查时、带有若干边界的区域：

blocks.en: Now here's the same region with edge probing:
blocks.zh: 下面这张是同一片区域、开了边界探查之后的样子：

blocks.en: As pleased as I am with this, I'd be surprised if there weren't significantly better algorithms for sampling the boundary, and I look forward to trying a few more methods in the future.
blocks.zh: 虽然我对这个结果挺满意，但如果说不存在明显更好的边界采样算法，我反而会吃惊。以后我很期待再试几种别的做法。
早期战果
blocks.en: Early Victories

Even with little development time, and the resulting rather simplistic code, Walk Monster already produces very usable output that can find real problems in the game.  Here are just a few examples of problems I've noticed in passing while developing the algorithm:
blocks.zh: 虽然开发时间很短、代码也因此相当简陋，Walk Monster 已经能产出非常好用的结果，找出游戏里的真实问题。下面只是我在开发这个算法过程中顺手注意到的几个例子：

blocks.en: The slopes on the side of this extended platform should not have been walkable, but they were.  This was because the player movement code has a pathologically bad way in which it deals with sloping geometry.  I now know that's in there, and I'll be sure to fix it when the time comes to bulletproof it.
blocks.zh: 这个加长平台侧面的斜坡本不该能走上去，但玩家能走。原因在于玩家移动代码处理倾斜几何体的方式病态地糟糕。现在我知道那里埋着这么一个东西，等到真正给它穿防弹衣的时候，我一定会修掉。

blocks.en: [The Witness](http://the-witness.net/news/) is meant to be a contemplative game, but wondering why there seemed to be a rock where there was no rock was not meant to be one of its koans.  As you might guess, this was because someone left a collision volume in the game when the geometry it represented had already been removed.  This is an easy thing to have happen, and it's nice to have a tool that trivially reveals these mistakes quickly so people don't have to worry about it.
blocks.zh: 《The Witness》确实是款让人沉思的游戏，但「明明没有石头，为什么这里像是有一块石头」并不该是它的公案之一。你可能已经猜到：有人删掉了某块几何体，却把代表它的碰撞体留在了游戏里。这种事很容易发生，而有一个能轻松快速暴露这类错误的工具是件好事，大家就不必再为它操心。

blocks.en: These were supposed to be impenetrable rocks, but Walk Monster revealed them to be anything but.  What's worse, Walk Monster revealed that the path was somehow only traversible in one direction (from left to right in this top-down screenshot), which is never supposed to happen.  I haven't actually looked at this problem yet, besides verifying that I could actually do it via player motion (I could).  It'll be interesting to see what's going on!
blocks.zh: 这些本该是无法穿越的岩石，但 Walk Monster 显示它们完全不是。更糟的是，Walk Monster 还发现这条路径居然只能单向通行（在这张俯视截图里是从左到右），而这永远不该发生。除了确认我真的能用玩家操作走过去（确实能），这个问题我还没细看。到底是怎么回事，挺让人好奇的！
待解的问题
blocks.en: Open Questions

It's encouraging to already have good results upon which we can build.  Like I said, if you pick the right name for your source files, it all flows smoothly from there!  But all of this work was done in the span of a few days, so it is obviously far from comprehensive and at lot of things are still completely ad hoc.  If I have time to develop these systems further, there are a number of questions worth answering.
blocks.zh: 已经有可以继续往上搭的好结果，这让人很受鼓舞。就像我说的，源文件名起对了，后面一切都会顺畅地流出来！但这些工作都是在几天之内完成的，所以显然远谈不上完备，很多东西还完全是临时凑的。如果我有时间把这些系统继续做下去，有几个问题值得回答。

blocks.en: First, what kinds of post-processing on the data should I do to make it easiest to visualize?  Drawing the raw network of points and edges can be very difficult for people to visually untangle, and some sort of better representation might make it possible for people to quickly understand more complex walkable areas at a glance.
blocks.zh: 第一，我该对数据做哪些后处理，才能让它最容易可视化？直接把原始的点与边网络画出来，人眼很难理清；换成某种更好的表示方式，也许就能让人一眼看懂更复杂的可行走区域。

blocks.en: Second, how can I improve the sampling patterns around boundaries to ensure that I find the most number of holes?  Are there good methods for characterizing the ways in which shapes fall into a lattice, and are there good tessellation schemes that maximize the chances of intersecting and passing through these shapes?
blocks.zh: 第二，我该如何改进边界周围的采样格局，以保证找出最多的漏洞？是否存在刻画「形状如何落进格点阵」的好方法，是否存在能最大化「与这些形状相交并穿过它们」概率的优秀细分方案？

blocks.en: Third, are regular sampling patterns or randomized sampling patterns better for filling spaces?  I could easily modify the target point selection criteria to produce randomized patterns, but it's not clear if this is worthwhile or, if it is, what kind of randomized patterns would be best.
blocks.zh: 第三，填充空间时，规则采样格局与随机采样格局哪个更好？我可以很轻松地修改目标点选取规则来产生随机格局，但目前不清楚这是否值得做，也不清楚如果值得，哪种随机格局最好。

blocks.en: Fourth, what other information would we like to get from our walkable area maps, now that we can build them?  For example, it would be a straightforward extension of the existing system to do things like pathfinding or distance mapping, where a user could pick a point and ask for the shortest path between it and some other point, or to see a heat map of the distance between that point and all other points in the map.  Are queries like this useful?  What other queries might be?
blocks.zh: 第四，既然现在能构建可行走区域地图了，我们还希望从这些地图里得到哪些别的信息？举例来说，在现有系统上做寻路或距离映射是很直接的扩展：使用者可以选定一个点，要求得到它与另一个点之间的最短路径，或者查看它到地图上所有其他点的距离热力图。这类查询有用吗？还可能有哪些别的查询？

blocks.en: For now, the walkable area visualizations we're already getting from Walk Monster are more than enough to show us that the player movement code is pretty broken.  I had planned to move on to creating a system for overnight testing via the user input method, but it seems clear that we already have enough problems to fix that there's no need for that yet.  So my next order of business, before improving these tools any further, will be to see what I can do to make the player movement code more robust.  While I'm at it, I'd also like to see if I can get it an order of magnitude faster or two, because currently, the thing that slows down Walk Monster rather severely is the slow speed of the collision system.
blocks.zh: 就目前而言，Walk Monster 已经给出的可行走区域可视化，足以说明玩家移动代码坏得相当厉害。我原本打算接着做一个用合成输入做整夜长跑的测试系统，但显然我们要修的问题已经够多了，暂时用不着它。所以在进一步完善这些工具之前，我的下一件事是看看能把玩家移动代码做得健壮到什么程度。顺便，我还想看看能不能让它快上一到两个数量级——因为眼下严重拖慢 Walk Monster 的，正是碰撞系统那缓慢的速度。

blocks.en: With luck, I'll report back soon in another installment on how that work is going.
blocks.zh: 运气好的话，我会在下一篇里汇报这项工作的进展。
